Microsoft Dynamics 365  |  Agentic CRM Briefing

Dynamics 365 in
the agentic era

CRM is moving from a system of record that people maintain to a system of intelligence that agents keep current, so sellers can spend their time selling.

What changes

Agents research, capture, enrich and recommend inside the CRM, and the seller stays in charge of the judgment calls.

Where it shows up

In Dynamics 365 Sales, and in Microsoft 365 Copilot, Cowork, Outlook and Teams, grounded in business data and Work IQ context.

Why it matters now

The return on AI comes from redesigning end-to-end processes, not from adding a chatbot to the old ones.

The productivity lesson

The opportunity is in reimagining business processes

Personal Computers →  Business Process Reengineering
Agentic AI →  Business Process Reimagining

The timeline is illustrative. It frames a hypothesis, not a forecast.

The constraint

AI is changing how work gets done. Core processes still have to run.

💸

Migration cost

Moving off legacy platforms is expensive, which slows the move to AI-ready systems.

🧩

Fragmented context

Data and context are spread across systems, so agents lack a complete picture.

❓

Unclear ROI

Adding AI to existing workflows rarely produces a clear, measurable return on its own.

⚖️

Inconsistent governance

Policies differ by app, which makes scaling agents risky.

The implication: agents need intelligence (shared context) and trust (consistent governance) before they can transform a mission-critical process.

Sources: IDC InfoBrief (Nov 2025) and Gartner (Feb 2026).

Agent 01 · Sales Qualification Agent

Qualify more of the leads you already have

Generally available
FunctionResearches leads, engages hundreds with personalized email, and finds the ones ready to buy.
WhereLead records, the Leads grid and the supervisor dashboard.
ScenarioWebinar leads arrive overnight. By morning, every lead is researched and the qualified ones are handed off.
ValueWider coverage, faster follow-up, more time on qualified conversations.
Why now

Too many leads, too few touched

0

of seller research workflows will begin with AI by 2027, up from less than 20% in 2024

Gartner, Innovation Insight: Invest in AI-Led Sales Research to Unlock Buyer Insights, 9 Oct 2024.

FromToWith
Priority overloadFocus on the hottest leadsContinuous, proactive research
Manual lead pursuitBetter-targeted interactionsPersonalized outreach at scale
Missed opportunitiesNo lead left unprocessedAutonomous next best actions

Pipeline targets are going up and headcount isn't, so there are more leads than a team can work by hand.

Autonomy

Choose how much autonomy the agent has

Assistive

Research-only

  • Researches leads that match source, rating and geography
  • Surfaces background, opportunities and company news
  • Assesses fit against your target profile
  • Drafts outreach for the seller to review and send
Best when sellers prefer to engage leads themselves.
→
Autonomous

Research and engage

  • Everything in research-only, plus autonomous outreach
  • Engages, follows up and evaluates BANT and handoff rules
  • Hands over only leads that show purchase intent
  • Disqualifies the rest and alerts a supervisor
Best when you have lead volume to take off sellers' plates.

You can move from research-only to research and engage, but you can't switch back. You can't delete a configured agent without Microsoft support.

Workflow

From new lead to qualified handoff

1Lead createdA new lead is added to the CRM.
2Agent pickupPicks up leads in scope.
3ResearchUses the public sources sellers checked by hand.
4OutreachPersonalized email from research and your value proposition.
5HandoffQualified leads routed to a seller with full context.
6SupervisionEscalates blockers to a supervisor, then resumes.
Handoff, research-only: high or medium fit goes to the seller. Low fit is disqualified and a supervisor is alerted.
Handoff, research and engage: the seller gets the lead once profile and BANT criteria are met, or the lead shows purchase interest.

Agent 03 · Data Enrichment Agent

Keep CRM records current from customer conversations

Generally available
FunctionAnalyzes recent emails and Teams meetings, links them to records and suggests (or applies) updates with a cited source.
WhereThe Data Enrichment pane on records, and the Suggested actions carousel.
Scenario"Budget is now $500K, target October." The agent suggests both updates, citing the meeting.
ValueAccurate records, less manual entry, more confidence in forecasts.
The gap

The latest details are in the conversation, not the record

📧 Email"Budget is now $500K."
🎥 Teams meeting"We are targeting October."
Manual updates are easy to delay and missData Enrichment Agent
The CRM record
BudgetNot captured$500K cited · email
Close datePrevious estimateOctober cited · meeting
Next stepNot capturedSuggested review & accept

Illustrative scenario.

In the record

Conversations become suggestions sellers review

  • Keeps job title, phone, industry and employee count up to date
  • Spots new stakeholders and suggests creating or linking records
  • Cites the source conversation so sellers can check each update

Suggestions are generated about every four hours and kept for 180 days. Meeting citations are visible only to attendees. Opportunities and leads get field suggestions; contacts get five fixed fields; accounts get activity linking only. Automatic updates are off by default.

Account planning

Account plans go stale. Make the plan a teammate.

How it used to be

📄 Frozen document

  • Written once, then frozen. A post-QBR snapshot that decays daily.
  • Cut off from the signals. The data that could catch a slip lived elsewhere.
  • Maintained by hand, so it wasn't. Plan and reality drift apart.
→
How it's being reinvented

✨ Living plan

  • AI drafts a cited position from your signals.
  • The seller decides, approving, editing or rejecting every time.
  • The CRM keeps it, as data in Dynamics 365, not a document.
  • Cowork drives it, so knowing becomes doing.

Roadmap Account planning is a roadmap direction. Parts are prototypes or in private preview.

CRM (Dynamics 365 Sales)Accounts, contacts, opportunities
Customer InsightsLifetime value, churn, similar accounts
Work IQWho met, emailed and chatted

Opportunity researchDeal risk, competitive intel
Next best actionsRecommended next steps
Sales Research Agentcomposes and cites the plan
→ The account plan: durable, native, cited, stored in Dataverse. Workplace signals sit next to business data, so the plan reflects the real relationship.

Recommended Actions

The decision & orchestration layer for sales

1 · UnifiedEvery actionable signal, from first-party agents, email and meeting insights and custom agents, lands in one place.
2 · PrioritizedOne ranked list of the few actions that matter today, each with a clear "why now".
3 · In the flow of workSales Home starts the day with one ranked list. The opportunity grid shows the top action on each record.
Scoring

From 100+ action cards to the seven that matter today

0action cards · 50+ records · 8-hour day
0ranked actions, each with "why now"
U · UrgencyHow soon must we act? Highest weight.
I · ImpactWhat's at stake? Deal size, strategic account, late stage.
C · ConfidenceHow reliable is the evidence? Decision-maker, budget, BANT.
E · EffortHow hard is it to do? Lowest weight.
Gating: Will it get worse if we wait? Is there a real downside if ignored? Both yes → surfaced everywhere. Each card carries 27 signals, from deal value to competitor mentions.

Customer 360 · The shift

From rebuilding a record to reading a customer picture

TodayThe classic form shows every field, but none of them says what matters.

Context layer

A context layer, not another agent

What it is

One governed view of the customer, assembled from the Dataverse records you already own. Account and Contact come first.

What it isn't

An agent competing for attention, a CDP or a migration. It works alongside what you run.

Where it fits

Every agent asks who this customer is. Customer 360 answers once, so the answers stop disagreeing.

Status

Private preview

Runs on customer Dataverse environments. Screens are design direction.

Why now

Not a data problem. A repetition problem.

1

The picture is spread out, and no single place holds the customer.

2

Every surface assembles its own reading of the same records.

3

The data model doesn't explain itself. The meaning lives with people.

4

It repeats for each entity: solved once, then again next door.

👔 Sellers

Prepare across several tools; what matters ends up in personal notes.

📣 Marketers

Hold engagement and intent data that rarely reaches the seller in context.

🎧 Service reps

Hunt for commercial facts from a read-only seat, then message the owner.

How it works

One governed context, assembled once, in four layers

GovernedActionsThe recommended next step, its approval and the outcome written back into the workflow.
GroundedEvidenceThe records behind each signal, so people can check it rather than trust it blindly.
ComputedInsightsEngagement, service burden, account posture and relationship risk, calculated once rather than per surface.
RecordAttributesAccounts and contacts stay the editable source of operational truth.
Trust metadata (source, freshness, confidence and missing data) travels with every layer. Operational truth stays separate from computed judgment.
Account 360

Make the account readable

  • Account posture: where the relationship stands
  • Relationship map: who's engaged and who's missing
  • Pipeline context: the commercial picture in the record
  • Service signals: support burden that changes the picture
  • Guided action: a governed next step with evidence
Contact 360

The person, in context

  • Contact info: who they are, role and tenure
  • AI overview: what to know before engaging
  • Insights & actions: what moves the relationship
  • Timeline: who engaged, with what, and sentiment
  • What's next: what's coming and how to prepare
Configuration

Governed edits, not custom forms

  • Structure by question: sections answer questions
  • Typed blocks: hero, insight card, fields, timeline, map
  • Design with AI: describe a change, review the diff
  • Validation & versioning: errors before publishing

Admins manage an insights catalog in Dataverse. Draft and test don't change anything live; publishing is the activation boundary. Scope sets where an insight is computed; it isn't a security role.

Adoption

A simple path from pilot to organization-wide adoption

1Executive alignmentAgree on outcomes: pipeline, productivity, conversion, forecast accuracy.
2Process assessmentFind where qualification, opportunity work and research happen today.
3Pilot launchRoll out Qualification and Opportunity agents to a limited group.
4Champion networkRecruit managers and top sellers as advocates.
5TrainingRole-based training, example prompts, handoffs and governance.
6Human-in-the-loopDefine what agents do alone and what sellers approve.
7Measure valueTrack leads, progression, time saved, win and conversion rates vs. baseline.
8ScaleMore agents, business units, geographies and sales motions.
9LeadershipManagers reinforce agent-driven selling behaviors.

Phases 1–5 launch the pilot. Phases 6–9 scale it. Measures are proposed for testing, not outcomes already achieved.
